overview.help.label: What is {term}?
overview.help.totals: We add up the documents that have passed review. Each document counts on the date of supply, or otherwise on its issue date.
overview.help.vat_calendar_year: If your income for a calendar year goes over {limit}, you become a VAT payer from 1 January. Then you add VAT to your prices and file a VAT return.
overview.help.vat_immediate: If your income for a year goes over {limit}, you are a VAT payer from the next day. You need to register right away.
overview.help.pausalni_dan_band: Flat-rate tax has three bands based on income. If your income goes over your band limit ({limit}), you pay more for the year.
overview.help.pausalni_dan_eligibility: You can have flat-rate tax only while yearly business income stays under {limit}. Above it you go back to the regular tax return.
overview.help.pausalni_vydaje_cap: Flat-rate expenses are a percentage of your income, but only up to a point. Above {limit} of income they stop growing.
overview.help.kind.vat_return: VAT payers tell the tax office how much VAT they collected and paid. They send the difference to the tax office account on the same day.
overview.help.kind.kh: The control statement is a list of invoices with VAT that VAT payers send along with the VAT return. The office uses it to compare invoices between companies.
overview.help.kind.pausalni_dan_advance: Flat-rate tax is one monthly payment that covers income tax, social and health insurance. You send it to the tax office account.
overview.help.kind.social_advance: Each month you send a social insurance advance to the social security office. We show the lowest possible amount, you may pay more.
overview.help.kind.health_advance: Each month you send a health insurance advance to your insurer. We show the lowest possible amount, you may pay more.
overview.help.kind.dap: Once a year you file the income tax return for last year. Filing it online is enough by the start of May.

help.ico: The IČO is an eight-digit number that every sole trader received when registering a trade. You will find it on your trade licence or on your invoices.
help.vat: A VAT payer adds tax to prices and pays it to the state. If you have never registered for VAT, you are not a payer – choose "No".
help.identifikovana_osoba: An identified person is not a VAT payer, but must pay VAT on some services bought from abroad, for example advertising on Facebook or Google. Choose this only if the tax office has confirmed it to you.
help.expenses: You can deduct expenses either by actual receipts or as a percentage of income. If you are not sure, choose "I don't know" – we will ask you later.
help.pausal_rate: The percentage depends on the trade: 80% crafts and agriculture, 60% other trades, 40% liberal professions, 30% rentals. You will find it in last year's tax return.
help.pausal_dan: Flat-rate tax is one monthly payment that covers income tax and social and health insurance. The band depends on your income and the type of activity.

vat.submit.title: How to submit
vat.submit.step1: Open MOJE daně (mojedane.gov.cz) and sign in with your bank identity or eObčanka.
vat.submit.step2: Choose Electronic forms, then Load from file.
vat.submit.step3: Load the VAT return first, then the control statement and the EC Sales List if you have them.
vat.submit.step4: Press Check and fix anything it reports.
vat.submit.step5: Press Submit and save the receipt with the submission number.
vat.submit.step6: Pay the VAT to your tax office's account, with your DIČ digits as the variable symbol. Then press I've filed it.
vat.submit.checked: Steps written from the official MOJE daně help. Labels on the site may differ slightly.
